title: Understanding k-fold Cross-Validation
text: In k-fold cross-validation, the dataset is divided into k subsets, and the model is trained k times, each time using a different subset as the validation set and the remaining as the training set.

title: Bias in k-fold Cross-Validation
text: Increasing k in k-fold cross-validation means that each model is trained on a larger portion of the data, which can reduce the bias of the model.

title: Computational Intensity of Cross-Validation
text: Cross-validation is generally more computationally intensive than regular validation because it involves training the model multiple times.

title: Using Entire Dataset in Cross-Validation
text: One advantage of cross-validation is that it allows the model to be tested on the entire dataset, providing a more comprehensive evaluation.
